summary: Walter William Skeat was a linguist who was educated at Highgate School, King's College School, and Christ's College, University of Cambridge. He later held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1878 to 1912.

Working in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz studied at Stanford University and the University of Oxford (Jesus College). He also studied as a disciple under Kazi Dawa Samdup around 1919–1921.

Walther Heissig worked in Central Asian, Tibetan, and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Vienna, Berlin, Göttingen, and Bonn, and held posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and the University of Bonn.

Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich and the University of Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann. He worked at the Prussian State Library and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1920–1951).

Walther Wüst worked in Indology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich, where he served as dean (1935–1945), and held posts at the Ahnenerbe and the Deutsche Akademie.
Wang Pachow was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied under Tan Yun-shan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wannaporn Rienjang, a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology, completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at the British Museum, University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).
Warren Cowgill was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Stanford University and Yale University. He served as a professor of linguistics at Yale University beginning in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who completed his PhD at Lancaster University (attested 2012) under doctoral supervisor Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad. He also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under supervisors Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, having also studied under Phra Sudhivorayan and Phramaha Somjin Sammāpañño.

Watari Yanai was a scholar in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1898 to 1901 and later held a post there from circa 1908 to 1926.

Wataru Mori, who worked in philosophy and other fields, studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1947–1951). He later held posts at Tokyo Medical and Dental University (circa 1968–1973) and the University of Tokyo (circa 1973–1989).

Wataru S. Ryose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, and also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances A. Wilson.

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned degrees from Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University. He taught at Fordham University before serving as Professor of Religion at Columbia University (circa 1972–2017).

Wei Lin is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Lin held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Western Michigan University, and Transylvania University.

Wei-jen Teng works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University, where Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil supervised his PhD, and teaches at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.

Weijue Shi was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Lingyuan (Linyuan) and Lingshuan. He founded Lin Quan Temple in 1987, Chung Tai Shan, and Chung Tai Buddhist Institute in 1993.

Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held teaching posts at the University of Hong Kong from circa 2002 to 2005 and at Renmin University of China from circa 2006 to 2019.
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).
Wen-ling Jane is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman, and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal.
